html:
Khozrugan (Z51) campaign chain

Region (English scoring table): East Cannor (Escann).

Formable country: Khozrugan (Z51)

One-line conclusion: Khozrugan reforges the ashes of the Greentide into a West Cannor conquest machine: strong armies, a direct route and rapid expansion, but a campaign almost entirely about war, coring and the next block of territory. The real difficulty is usually not winning battles, but managing aggressive expansion, administrative points and the ever-growing conquest list.

Story: Medium｜Mission-tree length: Long (36 dedicated missions)｜Mission-tree update: locally checked against v1.37.5.0｜Uniqueness: Medium-high｜Tedium: High｜Early pressure: Medium-high｜Expansion: Extremely high

Identity and formation

Khozrugan (Z51) is not an independent starting country in 1444. A qualifying green or grey Orc can form it through the “Reorganize the Western Army” decision; events associated with Unguldavor and Grombar can also release Khozrugan or let an ally change to Z51. [Local script][Local localization]

The direct formation route requires control of West Castanor, Feudalism, Administrative Technology 7, at least 10 provinces in the region and peace. After formation, it changes to green Orc culture, the Orcish Kingdom reform, Great Dookan worship and its dedicated mission tree. [Local script]

History and national story

The formable-country text builds Khozrugan's political memory on the Greentide: Korgus led the Orcs to the surface, defeated Castellyr and the states of East Cannor, but was stopped by Corin; after the leader's death, the united army broke into competing clans. [Local event text]

Z51 has no independent pre-1444 ruler sequence and no single scripted predecessor. The player is any power capable of reorganizing the Western Orcs. The central question is not “Who am I?” but “Who has the right to inherit the Greentide?”

The offline Wiki's short Khozrugan page describes it as a Rugan Orcish kingdom in West Castanor, ruled by Artug Ostokhan and inherited by Ornog Ostokhan, following Great Dookan and seeking a society governed by the strong. It lists the Venomtooth Clan as a predecessor; this explains the setting genealogy but cannot override the implemented formation decision, which allows multiple green or grey Orc countries to create Z51. [Wiki source][Local formation decision]

Related official diaries provide two narrative links. Issue 89 explains that Unguldavor can establish or control Khozrugan in the west; issue 106 calls the Venomtooth Clan a brutal precursor to Khozrugan. Neither is a Khozrugan-specific mission-tree diary, so Unguldavor or the Venomtooth Clan must not be presented as the only mechanical predecessor. [Related official development diaries]

Core mechanics

The Ostokhan duel. Formation creates a crisis of rule. The player can yield or accept a duel based on the monarch's military ability; victory can grant a permanent military modifier. It is a high-impact founding test, not a repeatable resource system. [Local script]

Clan subjects. Early missions require three high-opinion Orc subjects and temporarily increase their force limit. They can cover fronts and add troops, but relations, liberty desire and later integration still consume diplomatic resources. [Local script]

Military snowball. Ideas and missions concentrate on infantry, army tradition, morale, manpower, reinforcement, discipline and coring. Khozrugan has no high-frequency complex interface; its distinctiveness comes from the continuous sequence “formation–duel–clan war network–continental conquest.” [Local script]

Phased play

Before formation: prioritize Feudalism, Administrative Technology 7 and ten provinces in West Castanor, and make sure the last war ends with a rapid return to peace. The ruler's military ability affects the risk of the post-formation duel.

Early after formation: handle clan loyalty and the Ostokhan crisis before annexing every Orc subject. Three high-opinion subjects add troops and front coverage, creating a buffer for the westward war.

Middle game: missions direct the campaign toward Gawed, the Borderlands, Alenic lands and Ibevar. A single war is usually not the bottleneck; coring, aggressive expansion, the economy and idea progress are harder.

Late game: continue against Albaran, Esmaria, Dameria, Anbenncost and Corvuria, eventually dismantling Anbennar and unifying Cannor. Territorial objectives become longer and the gameplay more repetitive.

Mission future and end state

Khozrugan's mission future is to bring the divided clans back under central command, unify West Castanor, and carry Greentide-style warfare across Cannor. The mission text also presents conquest of Halann as a more distant political vision, but current scripts do not provide a complete global-conquest storyline. [Local script][Local event text]

Related developer replies once proposed retaining Great Dookan worship, adding a secular turn and strengthening the villain route. That is a future-design statement from the time, not proof that the current mission tree implements it. [Developer reply]

Personality and recommendation

The v2.1 personality coordinates are Expansion 100/100｜Authoritarianism 80/100｜Magic↔Artifice 50/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; thematic intensity 5/100)｜Pluralism 35/100.

The v2.1 values assessment is Neutral (47/100), with a stable trajectory. The available evidence strongly establishes extreme conquest, military obedience and a society of strength, but does not provide equally strong evidence for slavery, sacrifice, genocide or treating population as a resource. War and continental unification are not treated as evidence of evil by themselves.

Khozrugan is recommended for players who enjoy an infantry-heavy power, continuous wars, map painting and a clear continental endpoint. It is a poor fit for peaceful development, trade-colonial play, complex diplomacy, magic systems or many branching events.

Community experience

[Community view] A 2025 campaign-help thread focused on the Great Dookan route, West Cannor expansion, aggressive expansion and coring costs, showing that digesting expansion is a common pain point; it did not state an exact Mod version.

[Community view] A 2024 older-version AAR described the mission loop as “conquer–complete mission–receive new claims.” It predates the relevant Orc content update and is only a historical player impression.

Evidence boundary

This article covers the local base Mod and localization for v1.37.5.0, checked on 16 September 2026. The Tag, Chinese name, formation method, 36 missions, ideas and core mechanics come from the current local scripts and localization.

The local offline Wiki was reviewed for Khozrugan (page_id=1946, revision_id=29597) to supplement the rulers, culture, religion and Venomtooth genealogy; the page is a stub and cannot fill in the complete history. Two related official diaries and two player posts are also recorded; no Khozrugan-specific mission-tree development diary was found. The current Chinese name of capital 757 and a small number of mission details remain unresolved.

Full sources, page status and conflict records are on the evidence page.

National Ideas

The following reproduces the current local national-idea text and script effects. Traditions apply when the set is adopted; the seven ideas unlock in sequence as points are invested, and the ambition applies after all seven are unlocked. Only national ideas are listed: racial, government and mission bonuses are excluded. A successor idea set does not automatically stack with the earlier set. Idea descriptions may recall history or express future aspirations; they do not automatically establish events already completed in 1444. Names and complete descriptions use the current Mod’s English localisation. Alternative and predecessor/successor sets remain separately conditional, including whether new ideas are accepted on formation.

Effect units inherited from the source data are reproduced for parity, not revalidated here; suspicious percentages or script-valued effects require separate review. Raw script values are shown where appropriate.

Khozrugan (Z51) — Khozrugani Ideas

Set ID: Z51_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = {
        tag = Z51
    }

Khozrugani Traditions

  • Infantry Cost: -10% (infantry_cost; raw value -0.1).

  • Infantry combat ability: +15% (infantry_power; raw value 0.15).

1. Urak Dul

Urak Dul!

Once the warcry that broke kingdoms and peoples roared across these lands. But, after the bitter losses of Rottenstep and Castonath and the inglorious defeat of the Greentide, the battlefield no longer quakes with the bellows of orcish valor. Instead a festering doubt has taken hold in the minds of warriors, shamans, and chieftains alike. Was it a mistake to war against the humans? Was the Dookanson wrong?

Hah! These are the ponderings of weak-willed maggots! Are they true orcs? Or are they mewling warg pups? The past belongs to the forgotten. The present belongs to the living. And the future belongs only to those who will seize it.

  • Army tradition from battles: +0.5 (army_tradition_from_battle; raw value 0.5).

  • Unjustified demands: -20% (unjustified_demands; raw value -0.2).

2. Trample The Corpse of Wisdom

The living memory of the Greentide has all but faded away. And the times before, when our forebears roamed the caverns and tunnels of the Serpentspine, are nothing more than stories passed down. Yet there are those who still hold onto these bygone relics. Stubborn shamans who insist we “keep with the old ways”. Zealous fanatics who decry those of us who acknowledge Corin’s strength or look inward toward the orcish soul. Pithering fools all of them and soon to be tongueless. Tradition is the corpse of wisdom. Let it be buried alongside the rest of the dead.

  • Idea cost: -15% (idea_cost; raw value -0.15).

3. Cannor's Tombstone

“Built long ago, when the human empire of Castanor still stood, Bal Mire was built to watch over wild Alenic tribes. By the time of Khozrugan, the fabled fortress had fallen into disrepair and ruin, sinking into the swampy mud that it was built atop.

Its settlement as the capital of the newly formed Khozrugan and its refounding as Ur Morduba was amongst the boldest decisions made by the orcish state, for the orcs had focused on the wholesale destruction of fortresses rather than restoration. It proved a wise decision when the war with the adventuring companies of Cobalt Company and Brave Brothers began. Many an adventurer would see their demise in the swampy surrounds…”

  • Khozrugan: A Legacy of the Greentide by Armyn Stynài, Chapter 2

  • Fort defense: +15% (defensiveness; raw value 0.15).

4. Osulband

To this day, even after generations, there are many amongst us who fail to recognize what the greatest spoil of victory is - land. It is the land that grows the foodstuffs that feed our clans. It is the land that supports the livestock our wargs feast on. It is the land that bears us the iron we need most for further conquests. But, the land does not offer this freely. Hands are needed to till, herd, and mine. Hands that are not always willing to provide as they should.

No matter, for we shall declare Osulband, the earthbinding. Those who are too weak to fight, shall be forever tied to the land. It is the finest honor we could ever grant, for they shall be the ones to tend to our greatest spoil.

  • National Supply Limit Modifier: +15% (global_supply_limit_modifier; raw value 0.15).

  • Production efficiency: +10% (production_efficiency; raw value 0.1).

5. Tazhor-u Bazu

“Tazhor-u Bazu, or demonstration of strength, is as old as the worship of Dookan himself. Before their arrival in Escann, during the more fractious days of the Serpentspine, the sport varied greatly across the clans. All forms of it involved some level of wrestling within a marked arena, but which moves were allowed or even what constituted victory was rarely defined.

While some standardization would occur within the unified Greentide, its core rules would not be settled until the founding of Khozrugan. Due its focus on dominance, victory would center around the submission of the opponent via grapples and takedowns with old tactics such as biting and punching being discouraged and eventually banned. Eventually the ruleset became popular to see adoption in Unguldavor and even distant Bramund.”

  • Khozrugan: A Legacy of the Greentide by Armyn Stynài, Chapter 7

  • Army morale: +15% (land_morale; raw value 0.15).

6. Daroosh Bloodfist

“Oi, you slacking off? Think you can get away with being lazy because I’m a halfling anbakh? Hey, where’d your smile go? Reminded me a lot of my predecessor’s ugly mug. Know what happened to him? No? Simple, I broke his skull in. Moment I caught him stealing from the crop, I tackled him down and smashed him til that smile was no more. Got to take his place soon after. No questions asked.

You see, Warchief’s got no tolerance for filth like that. And neither do I. So best you shape if you want to keep that smile of yours…”

-Daroosh Bloodfirst to an orcish farmhand

  • Yearly corruption: -0.05 (yearly_corruption; raw value -0.05).

  • Number of accepted cultures: +1 (num_accepted_cultures; raw value 1).

7. The Overseers

“Known as the Anbahk in orcish, the Overseers gradually came to as the labors of Osulband began to bear fruit. The loot and communal loyalty that once held the chieftains and clans’ the Khozrguan hierarchy collapsed giving rise to plantation retinues and serfs rather than warriors and clansmen rose.

While the arrangement was more akin to that of the era of Feudalistic Cannor than the rising centralized states of Age of Unraveling, it did enable the orcish state to quickly establish an administration that could support its expansionist tendencies and desires.”

  • Khozrugan: A Legacy of the Greentide by Armyn Stynài, Chapter 11

  • Liberty desire from subject development: -0.25 (liberty_desire_from_subject_development; raw value -0.25).

Khozrugani Ambition

  • Vassal force limit contribution: +100% (vassal_forcelimit_bonus; raw value 1).
